questions.q: Two circularly shaped linear polarisers are placed coaxially. The transmission axis of the first polarizer is at $30^{{}^{\circ}}$ from the vertical while the second one is at $60^{{}^{\circ}}$, both in the clockwise sense. If an unpolarised beam of light of intensity $\mathrm{I}=20 \mathrm{ W} / \mathrmm^{2}$ is incident on this pair of polarisers, then the intensities $\mathrm{I}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{I}_{2}$ transmitted by the first and the second polarisers, respectively, will be close to
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \mathrm{I}_{0} &=20 \mathrm{ W} / \mathrmm^{2} \\ \mathrm{I}_{1} &=\frac{\mathrm{I}_{0}}{2}=\frac{20}{2}=10 \mathrm{ W} / \mathrmm^{2} \\ \mathrm{I}_{2} &=\mathrm{I}_{1} \cos ^{2} 30^{{}^{\circ}} \\ &=10\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^{2}=10 . \frac{3}{4} \\ &=7.5 \mathrm{w} / \mathrmm^{2} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, the amplitudes of the two waves incident on the two slits are $A$ and $2A$. If ${I}_{0}$ is the maximum intensity, then the intensity at a spot on the screen, where the phase difference between the two interfering waves is $ϕ$.
questions.solution:
Resultant intensity when two waves with phase difference $ϕ$ interfere is

$I = {I}_{1} + {I}_{2} + 2\sqrt{{I}_{1}}\sqrt{{I}_{2}}cosϕ$

As, intensity $I ∝ A^{2} or I = kA^{2},$

where $k = a$ constant and A$ is amplitude.

So, $I = {A}_{1}^{2} + {A}_{2}^{2} + 2{A}_{1}{A}_{2}cosϕ$

Here, ${A}_{1} = A and {A}_{2} = 2A$

$⇒ I = A^{2} + $\left(2A\right)^{2}$ + 2 $\left(A\right)\left(2A\right)cosϕ$

$= A^{2}\left(5 + 4cosϕ\right)........(i)

Intensity is maximum \left({I}_{0}\right),$

when $cosϕ = 1$

$⇒ {I}_{0} = A^{2}\left(5 + 4 \times1\right) =$9A^{2}$

$⇒ A^{2} = {I}_{0} / 9$.......(ii)

So, resultant intensity,

$I = A^{2} $\left(5 + 4cosϕ\right)$

[From Eqs. (i) and (ii)]

$⇒ I = \dfrac{I0}{9}\left(5 + 4cosϕ\right)$

$tan\theta = 0. 93$

time to cross this region $= \dfrac{2Dtan\theta}{ speed }$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, the distance between the two slits is $0.1 \mathrm{ mm}$, the distance between the slits and the screen is $1 \mathrm{ m}$ and the wavelength of the light used is $600 \mathrm{ nm}$. The intensity at a point on the screen is $75 \%$ of the maximum intensity. What is the smallest distance of this point from the central fringe?
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{d}=0.1 \mathrm{ mm}, \mathrm{D}=1 \mathrm{ m}, \lambda=600 \mathrm{ nm}\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{p}}=75 \%$ of maximum or $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{p}}=3 \mathrm{I}_{0}$
Where $I_{0}$ is the intensity of a single wave
now $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{P}}=3 \mathrm{I}_{0}=\left(\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{0}}\right)^{2}+\left(\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{0}}\right)^{2}+2 \sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{0} \times \mathrm{I}_{0}} \cos \phi\therefore \cos \phi=\cos \frac{\pi}{3}$, also $\Delta \mathrm{x}=\frac{\mathrm{yd}}{\mathrm{D}}$
now $\Delta \mathrm{x}=\frac{\lambda}{2 \pi} \times \frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{\lambda}{6} \quad \therefore \mathrm{y}=\frac{\lambda \mathrm{D}}{6 \mathrm{ d}}=\frac{600 \times 10^{-9} \times 1}{6 \times 0.1 \times 10^{-3}}$ or $\mathrm{y}=1 \mathrm{ m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Unpolarised red light is incident on the surface of a lake at incident angle ${θ}_{R}$. An observer seeing the light reflected from the water surface through a polariser notices that on rotating the polariser, the intensity of light drops to zero at a certain orientation. The red light is replaced by unpolarised blue light. The observer sees the same effect with reflected blue light at incident angle ${θ}_{B}$.

Then,
questions.solution:
As intensity of reflected light changes on rotating the polaroid this means reflected beam is polarised.

By Brewster's law,

$n = tan\theta$

${n}_{Blue} > {n}_{Red}$

$⇒ tan{θ}_{B} > tan{θ}_{R}$

$⇒ {θ}_{B} > {θ}_{R}$

Also, from geometry of figure, $\theta > 45 °$.

So, we have ${θ}_{B} > {θ}_{R} > 45 °$.
